info.title: CivicOS platform API
info.description: Every HTTP endpoint of this installation, generated from its route files (scripts/build-openapi.mjs). Request and response bodies are JSON, typed from the TypeScript types the routes use where they declare them; errors are `{ "error": string }`. Sign-in rules follow the platform middleware and lib/auth/roles.ts: public sites and public reads are open, everything else needs an official's session or the machine credential named in each operation's security. `x-permission-rule` names the rule a change falls under (administrator, ministry, official, bearer, self-authenticated, public-write).

post.description: /api/admin/officers/bulk — server-side bulk officer onboarding. Accepts a CSV or JSON array of {email,name,charter_id,role,title?} and forwards to civicos_admin_bulk_create_officers via the service-role client. Returns the substrate's per-row result so the UI can show which entries succeeded and which failed. Auth: callers must hold a platform-tier session OR pass the CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET (so CLI/automation can use it without a UI sign-in). The substrate enforces the platform-tier check separately, so this route is a defense-in-depth gate, not the sole authorisation.

The AI advisory for a console panel (per-nation opt-in; register 2.1). The body is validated (lib/ai/advisory-input.ts: types, ranges, a label cap, control characters stripped), each figure carries its SignalKind and the prompt tells the model which figures are samples. Every call is audited: who asked, the model, SHA-256 of the prompt and of the answer, and whether the model or the rule-based fallback answered. The request is operational data leaving the platform, so it goes through the data-sovereignty gate (lib/data/sovereignty.ts, category 'ai-advisory': off unless a named official enabled it); when it is off the panel gets the rule-based advisory and nothing is sent. The model service is the nation's choice (SovereignProfile.aiAssistantModel: the default provider or its own sovereign / on-premises model; lib/ai/model.ts). Each official may ask CIVICOS_AI_RPM times a minute (default 10).

source.description: Who answered: the model, or the rule-based fallback. Only 'model' may be shown as "AI advisory".

get.description: /api/audit/proof — single-entry verifiable inclusion proof. Given (scope, seq) the endpoint returns: - The audit chain prefix from genesis to seq, so a verifier can re-walk every prev_hash → hash relationship locally. - The targeted entry (== the last row in the prefix). - Every witness attestation that observed (scope, seq), so the verifier can confirm the recorded hash matches what witnesses saw at that time. - A server timestamp framing the proof. The output is the same shape the /api/substrate/export endpoint produces, so it loads directly into /gov/audit-replay (or any third-party copy of lib/audit/replay.ts). Auth: public read. Audit entries are already publicly readable per the RLS policy on civicos.audit_entries.

Passwords of platform accounts (lib/auth/officials.ts). POST { action: 'change', current, next }: the signed-in official changes their own; every other session of theirs ends and this one is renewed. POST { action: 'reset', email, code, next }: no session; sets a new password with the one-time code an administrator issued (wrong codes count toward the sign-in lockout). get.description: The signed-in official's second sign-in step (authenticator app, RFC 6238; lib/auth/officials.ts). GET: whether it is on, whether the installation requires it, and the policy. POST { action }: 'start' → a new key (shown once) and its otpauth:// link; 'confirm' { code } → turns it on, returns ten recovery codes (shown once) and renews the session as having passed the second step; 'off' { code } → turns it off (not when the policy requires it); 'policy' { policy: none | signers | all } → administrators only. Every change is audited. Platform accounts only: substrate officers use the substrate's own sign-in.

The nation's own boundaries (lib/data/boundaries.ts): GET lists every version (without shapes); POST checks a boundary file (?dryRun=1 records nothing) and records it as a proposal for a different official to publish. get.description: Audit-chain anchoring cron — periodically broadcasts the head of every visible audit scope as a federation event of type 'audit.anchor' on channel 'constitutional'. External systems that subscribe to the federation stream get a continuous live record of where each chain pointed at known wall-clock times. Complements the witness-attestation system: - audit_witnesses table is the append-only, public, tamper-proof record (provable retroactively). - federation 'audit.anchor' events are the realtime broadcast channel (subscribers see it as it happens; consumers can persist externally for an independent record). The platform's own chain (lib/data/store.ts) is anchored too: its head is signed (lib/audit/sign.ts), written to the append-only anchor file outside the state (file mode, lib/audit/anchor.ts) and, with the substrate connected, broadcast as scope 'platform' with its signature. Without the substrate only the platform head is anchored. With CIVICOS_TSA_URL the head is first time-stamped by the nation's RFC 3161 TSA (lib/audit/tsa.ts) and the token travels with it. Auth: CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET via ?token=… or Authorization: Bearer. Cadence: every 5–15 minutes. Idempotent — anchoring the same head produces an event with the same content, but federation events are append-only so duplicate broadcasts are allowed (consumers dedupe by (scope, seq) if they care).

get.description: Outbound federation webhook delivery worker. For each active civicos.event_webhooks row, finds federation events on its channel newer than its cursor and POSTs each to the registered URL with an HMAC-SHA256 signature header. On an all-2xx run the cursor advances to the last delivered event's at_ms; on the first failure the cursor holds (so the next run retries from the same point) and the failure is recorded. Auth: CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET via ?token=… or Authorization: Bearer. Delivery is at-least-once per cursor; consumers dedupe on event id. Cadence: recommended every 1–5 minutes.

get.description: Periodic consent auto-expiry. Citizens grant time-bound consents (`expires_at` in the future); past expiry they should flip to 'expired' so officer-side surfaces see them as no-longer-valid and the citizen's wallet doesn't show them as live. civicos.expire_due_consents performs the flip and writes one audit-chain entry per expired consent on the citizen's scope, so the citizen can trace exactly which consent expired and when. Auth: CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET via ?token=… or Authorization: Bearer. Cadence: recommended hourly.

get.description: Per-charter posture aggregator. Reads each activated institution's open pressure (work items + escalations + dispatches), derives a posture / readiness / stress reading, and appends a posture_history snapshot. Designed to run on a slow cadence (every 30 minutes or so); produces a continuous timeline visible on /gov/posture without requiring any operator to manually snapshot. The activated institutions come from the platform's register (lib/institution/charter-register.ts; architecture review D8), not from the substrate's civicos.institutions, which only mirrors it; the pressure counts are the substrate's own rows.

get.description: Periodic directive-promotion worker. Directives are the platform's register (lib/data/directives.ts, architecture review D8): this flips every directive signed for a future effective date to 'effective' once that date arrives (reads settle them too; this makes it happen without one), then, with the substrate connected, re-copies the platform's directives and institutions to their substrate mirrors (lib/db/mirror.ts: retries anything a write after a change could not copy). Designed for a scheduler (pg_cron in supabase/cron/schedule.sql, Vercel Cron, …). The substrate's own civicos_promote_due_directives is no longer called: its table is a mirror. Protection: shared CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET via ?token=… or Authorization: Bearer. The secret never reaches the client bundle (server-only route).

get.description: Update watchdog cron — every minute (supabase/cron/schedule.sql). Concludes due probations for every nation: passes a release whose window ended healthy, records overdue health reports as missing, and on a confirmed failure either switches the software back to the last known good release or leaves it waiting for the nation's decision (ask-first, or a release that is not backward compatible). It never installs anything: it can only conclude probations and switch back to the last known good release. The same evaluation also runs when the chamber, a release, the publisher console or the health endpoint is read, as a fallback if the schedule stops. Auth: CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET as `Authorization: Bearer …` (or ?token=), like every /api/cron/* worker.

get.description: Tamper-detection watchdog. Runs after witness-sweep on the same cadence (or slower) and looks for any audit scope where a recorded attestation disagrees with the live chain. Each divergence becomes: 1. A `civicos.escalations` row at severity 'major', source 'substrate', reason 'witness-divergence:<scope>'. 2. A `civicos.federation_events` entry on channel 'constitutional', type 'audit.divergence', so any subscribed watcher sees it. Auth: CIVICOS_CRON_SECRET via ?token=… or Authorization: Bearer. Cadence: every 15 minutes (same as witness-sweep, but staggered). Idempotent: re-recording the same divergence is silently deduplicated by escalation reason — the operator sees one row, not one per cron tick.

get.description: /api/health — diagnostic ping with a substrate reachability probe. Public (no auth) — returns minimal information so it's safe to expose to monitoring systems. Reports: ok flag, substrate-configured flag, substrate-reachable flag (via a cheap count on a public view), and where the platform keeps its state (lib/data/persist.ts): mode, last save, this server's role as state writer, who holds the writer's lease, and any error. Probes (Helm chart): `?live` answers at once without asking the substrate (liveness); `?ready` answers 503 while this server cannot take changes (a standby without the writer's lease, a writer that stopped saving, or a failed restore), so no traffic reaches it (readiness). Without either, the answer is always 200, as before. Also (counts only, nothing personal): the platform audit chain (entries, intact), twin sources overdue against their schedule, warnings and errors logged in the last hour, whether traces go to the nation's collector, and an overall status: ok, degraded (something needs attention but changes are safe) or down (changes are not safe). With CIVICOS_STATE=postgres, `persistence.database` reports the per-record tables (lib/data/repo/postgres.ts): the adapter, PostGIS, the write queue's depth, how far behind other instances' changes this one is (outbox lag) and any write error, and the per-record documents every other store is kept as (stores, records, merges). A standby there still serves reads and record changes (every change, once every store is in the tables: a follower), so it reports ready while its tables are healthy.

get.description: /api/public/accountability — open-data JSON for the published accountability aggregates (service SLAs, appeals pipeline, decision-time trends, institutional data-access footprint, governance output). Everything here is already anon-readable on the Public Observatory / charter profiles; this exposes it in a machine-readable form so journalists and researchers can consume it programmatically instead of scraping. Aggregate-only (no citizen id, ref, or row-level field). No auth — public by design — and short-cached. Query params: ?days=1..365 (default 90), ?charter=<charter_id> to scope, ?weeks=1..104 for the trends (default days/7), ?directive_days=1..1825 for the governance output (default 365), ?only=directives for that part alone (what the charter profile and the scoreboard read). Governance output (directive_stats, directive_trend) is computed from the platform's directives register, which owns directives (architecture review D8), not from the substrate's mirror of it; `directive_source` says so (lib/twin/signal.ts: reported, the platform's own record). The other aggregates are the substrate's own rows (requests, appeals, consents).

get.description: /api/public/charters — open-data directory of institutions (charters). Pairs with /api/public/accountability: researchers need the charter catalog (id, label, kind, domain) to interpret the per-charter SLA/appeals stats. Institutions are already public in the Government Directory; this is their machine-readable form. No auth; short-cached. Read from the register's owner only (architecture review D8): the platform's ministry registry and standing institutions (lib/institution/charter-register.ts), first-activation times included. The substrate's civicos.institutions mirrors them and is not read here. This is also the answer the console's charter screens read (charter list, profile and detail, institutions catalogue, observatory, search) through lib/db/repos/institutions.ts. Query: by default the activated charters (the directory as before); ?activated=any for every charter, ?activated=false for the idle ones; ?kind=<kind>, ?charter=<charter_id>, ?q=<text in id, label or domain>.

Read from the register's owner, the platform (lib/data/directives.ts); the substrate only mirrors it.

OGC API – Features items: the nation's subdivisions as GeoJSON with their observed values (?limit, ?offset, ?bbox=minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat, ?datetime, ?level=1|2), or the national facility register's published sites (also ?category), as the viewer may see them, or the published boundaries in force (also ?level). Each collection's queryables (/collections/{id}/queryables) are accepted as equality filters (e.g. ?regionCode=KE-30&status=operational); any other parameter is refused with 400. CQL2 filters (OGC API – Features Part 3): ?filter=<CQL2-Text or CQL2-JSON>&filter-lang=cql2-text|cql2-json&filter-crs=CRS84 on the queryables and geometry (lib/twin/cql2.ts); an invalid filter is 400 with the reason. Coordinate systems (Part 2, lib/twin/ogc-crs.ts): ?crs=<URI> serves the features in EPSG:4326, EPSG:3857 or one of the nation's national grids (each collection lists them in `crs`), ?bbox-crs=<URI> reads bbox in one of them; the answer's Content-Crs header names the system of its coordinates.

get.description: OGC SensorThings API v1.1 service root of the national twin (read-only): the entity sets (Things, Locations, Sensors, ObservedProperties, Datastreams, Observations) and the conformance classes served (lib/twin/sta.ts).

What the twin knew at a moment (?asOf=ISO time, default now): the latest value of each entity's metric recorded by then and true by then, with its source and run (lineage). ?knownAt= separates the two: true by asOf, as recorded by knownAt (e.g. knownAt=now for "true then, as known today"). Filter with ?metric= and ?entity=. A derived metric (lib/twin/derived.ts, e.g. population.share_65_plus) is computed from its inputs' observed values and answered as modelled, never observed: each value carries kind "modelled", the formula and the inputs it used (lib/twin/derived-server.ts); `derived` describes the formula.

One Mapbox Vector Tile (MVT 2.1) of the nation's boundaries: polygon layers "regions" (official subdivisions), "districts" (from zoom 5) and "disputed" (disputed territory near the nation, marked disputed unless the nation chose a point of view in setup; never assigned to a side by the platform). Shapes are the boundary versions in force, read as every map reads them (loadNationGeography() / loadDistricts(), lib/twin/boundary-tiles.ts). The ETag changes when another boundary version comes into force, so a client revalidating with If-None-Match gets 304 until then. Zoom 0–14; y may end in .mvt or .pbf. Behind the official's session, or a GIS client's integration key or access token of scope ogc:read.

get.description: The national facility register as one PMTiles v3 archive (vector layer "facilities", zoom 0–12 by default), read with HTTP range requests (Range: bytes=a-b → 206 Partial Content; HEAD for the size and ETag). Open without sign-in: it holds only what the public may see — restricted sites at their generalised position, exactly as viewFacility() gives a viewer who is not signed in; confidential sites never. Rebuilt after publication changes (lib/twin/tiles-archive.ts) and kept as a file in the platform's data directory: a range request reads only the bytes it asks for from the file (in memory only where there is no writable directory). A new build has a new ETag, so a reader can tell its ranges came from one build (If-Range is honoured). Signed-in officials read the viewer-aware tiles at /api/twin/tiles/facilities/{z}/{x}/{y}.mvt, and an institution's own archive at /api/org/ministries/{id}/facilities/tiles.pmtiles.

One Mapbox Vector Tile (MVT 2.1) of the national facility register: layer "facilities", published sites as points with their id, national id, name, category, status, region and certification. Restricted sites are placed where the viewer may see them (generalised for viewers without need), so a tile is private to its viewer. y may end in .mvt or .pbf (lib/twin/tiles.ts).

TileJSON 3.0.0 for the national facility register's vector tiles: the tile address template (/api/twin/tiles/facilities/{z}/{x}/{y}.mvt), zoom range, bounds of the sites the viewer may see and the layer's fields (lib/twin/tiles.ts).
The dates a metric has observations for (?metric=), oldest first: the steps of the twin's history view.

deliversRequests.description: Feature requests this build delivers (nation builds only).

platformReleaseId.description: The platform pipeline release this was promoted from, if any.

rollout.description: Staged rollout: pilot-ring nations first, then general availability.

compatibleWithPrevious.description: Its migrations leave the previous release working on the new schema (expand/contract), so the software can be switched back automatically without touching data. False forces "ask before falling back".

status.description: Publisher safety: a halted or withdrawn release cannot be newly approved or installed.

state.description: Awaiting a decision when the nation asked to decide before falling back.

dataRestored.description: Fallback switches software only. Restoring the data snapshot is a separate, deliberate decision.

installs.description: nationId → releaseId → state, for the install matrix.

promotable.description: Stable platform-pipeline releases not yet published to nations.

receivedAt.description: When the case reached the institution; its age is counted from this. Absent on examples.

source.description: Where the case came from: an example of the platform, a loaded file, typed in, or a connected case system. Absent means example.

feedId.description: The connected case system (CaseFeed) that sent it; only that system updates it.

importId.description: The load (lib/data/case-import.ts) a case came in with.

actedAt.description: When an official last assigned, escalated or closed it.

queueDepth.description: Changes written in memory and not yet committed.

rebased.description: Audit entries moved up the chain because another instance appended first.

followed.description: Outbox rows applied from other instances, the last one's id, and how far behind its commit time this instance applied it (ms).

api.description: The API that changes it (the only write path).

storage.description: How the owner's records are kept durably when it is not the store's JSON snapshot alone: with CIVICOS_STATE=postgres the persistence port (lib/data/repo) writes them through to per-record tables. The tables are the same register, not a copy.

mode.description: Delivery mode this artifact serves; 'any' for SBOMs, documentation and client apps.

ref.description: OCI reference for images and charts (pinned by digest).

placeholder.description: Always true in this build: the link serves a manifest, not a real binary.

pattern.description: Expand/contract keeps the previous release working on the new schema, so a fallback is clean; in-place changes rely on the restore point.

fallback.description: Automatic restores the last known good release on failure; ask waits for a decision.

healthSource.description: Who reports health: the in-store simulation (prototype) or the nation's deployment agent.

definitionsPolicy.description: Security definitions are data: applied automatically by default.

stagingRequired.description: A production install needs the same release to pass staging probation and a UAT sign-off (default on).

version.description: The version the snapshot protects (the release running when it was taken).

contents.description: Database snapshot, configuration, the previous release's artifacts.

restoreNotes.description: What restoring it gives back and what is lost (irreversible migrations).

interval.description: The projection at the low and high ends of the assumptions' ranges (modelled), when any assumption states a range.

asOf.description: The date the observed state was taken from (true on that date, as known when the version was made).

national.description: The regions combined as the metric says (sum or mean), only when every region has a value in one unit.

nationalNote.description: Why there is no national figure, when there is none.

horizon.description: The date the projection is for; when a value true for it is later observed, the error is logged (calibration).

metricDimension.description: The dimension that says what is measured (default: the first of INDICATOR, MEASURE, SERIES, CONCEPT, SUBJECT present).

codes.description: Explicit codes → registered metric ids, over the metrics' own SDMX concepts.

units.description: SDMX unit codes → UCUM (e.g. PS → {persons}); other units must already be the metric's unit.

registry.description: The office's SDMX REST API (e.g. https://stats.example.go.ke/rest), on the source's own host: structures are fetched from it.

dataflow.description: The dataflow the file belongs to, AGENCY:ID(VERSION): its DSD and code lists validate and label every run (lib/twin/sdmx-structure.ts).

SdmxStructureUse.description: What a run keeps of the structure it was checked against.

labels.description: For each coded component, the labels of the codes this run saw (at most LABELS_PER_COMPONENT each).

cvss.description: CVSS v3.1 base score and vector.

affectedFrom.description: Affected versions: from `affectedFrom` up to (not including) `affectedBefore`, or all later versions if absent.

status.description: final: fix available; interim: still under investigation.

dependency.description: Raised from the platform's own dependency audit (scripts/audit-deps.mjs), not written by hand.

baseline.description: Always-on protection every nation has, paid or not.

localPricing.description: False until a contract rate is set: quotes stay in the reference currency.

certified.description: Vendor certified by the publisher (placeholder names in this build).

tier.description: 'included': free and always on for every nation; 'paid': advanced tools licensed per unit. See StorePolicy.

certification.description: What the publisher tested before certifying the product, and against which platform versions.

placeholder.description: Vendor-neutral placeholder product: no real software is distributed.

automaticActive.description: Automatic updates run only while some protection is active.

unitPriceRef.description: Annual price per unit in the publisher's reference currency (major units).

SecurityGate.description: Advisory only: security coverage never blocks an update.

platformCovered.description: The platform estate is covered (Endpoint/EDR licence or estate-wide BYO with a fresh scan).

nationSoftwareCovered.description: The nation's own software is covered (any BYO or platform licence).

payment.description: 'transfer': government procurement (purchase order, invoice, bank transfer with a reference); 'instant': paid at once on the nation's rail; 'included': no charge.

installedVersion.description: Security software version the nation runs; upgrading it is the nation's decision.

certified.description: Vendor certified by the publisher (placeholder names in this build).

tier.description: 'included': free and always on for every nation; 'paid': advanced tools licensed per unit. See StorePolicy.

certification.description: What the publisher tested before certifying the product, and against which platform versions.

placeholder.description: Vendor-neutral placeholder product: no real software is distributed.

body.description: The body's name when the authority is "other", or its formal name.

legalBasis.description: The law or instrument the decision rests on, e.g. "Critical Infrastructure Protection Act 2019, s.12".

nations.description: Which nations it affects: every nation, or the ones listed.

scheduled.description: Planned maintenance (announced ahead; excluded from availability).

seq.description: Sequence number of the chain entry that was the head.

production.description: False when signed with the generated development key.

anchoredAt.description: Set by the anchor cron once the head was copied outside the platform state.

genTime.description: The time the TSA vouches for (ISO 8601).

serial.description: The token's serial number (hex) and policy OID.

trusted.description: The certificate chains to CIVICOS_TSA_CA (absent when none was configured).

tsa.description: The TSA, from its certificate (CN, O).

timestamp.description: "time-stamped by <tsa> at <genTime>" (RFC 3161), when the nation's TSA stamped it.

head.description: The last signed head, as checked.

timestamped.description: Heads time-stamped by the nation's TSA (each token checked again).

pending.description: Heads a remote key provider has not signed yet (not counted as evidence).

currentKey.description: The signed heads' key is the one configured now (CIVICOS_AUDIT_KEY or the key provider's).

minAreaKm2.description: The smallest triangle of three neighbouring points kept, in km² (Visvalingam's tolerance).

units.description: Units before and after (always the same).

alt.description: What the logo shows, for people who cannot see it.

headline.description: First line in ink, second in the site's primary colour.

crest.description: Glyph shown before the nation's insignia is set.

about.description: A sentence about the institution for the footer; the tagline when absent.

news.description: Announcements, newest first. Reference items are samples and carry no date.

newsSource.description: 'feed': taken from the ministry's existing website (Link, Embed or Migrate mode).

quickServices.description: The "I want to…" tasks; each opens a real service. Colour: a hex value or 'primary' / 'accent'.

statisticsSource.description: Where the figures come from. Reference figures are samples until the institution supplies its own.

content.description: Fields of the site's content; each replaces the published (or reference) field whole.

preset.description: A design preset the site may use; null returns to the site's default.

replace.description: Restoring an earlier version: the content replaces the published content entirely.

translation.description: Translations of the site's text into one language (string by string, each with its source).

translations.description: Restoring: the translations to put back in place of the published ones.

brand.description: The ministry's own colours and logo; null removes them.

id.description: The site's route segment, e.g. 'police' for /police.

crest.description: Glyph shown before the nation's insignia is set.

about.description: A sentence about the institution for the footer; the tagline when absent.

headline.description: First line in ink, second in the site's primary colour.

quickServices.description: The "I want to…" tasks; each opens a real service. Colour: a hex value or 'primary' / 'accent'.

statisticsSource.description: Where the figures come from. Reference figures are samples until the institution supplies its own.

news.description: Announcements, newest first. Reference items are samples and carry no date.

newsSource.description: 'feed': taken from the ministry's existing website (Link, Embed or Migrate mode).

version.description: 0 = the reference record, nothing published by the nation yet.

items.description: The last good copy: kept when a later fetch fails.

locale.description: The nation's language, which the site is translated into.

lang.description: The page's language: the nation's once most of its text is translated, else English.

dir.description: Right to left only when every string is translated into a right-to-left language.

summary.description: What the proposal changes, in words.

basedOn.description: The published version this proposal was made against.

preset.description: The design preset chosen for this site (one its sector allows); the site's default when unset.

headline.description: First line in ink, second in the site's primary colour.

crest.description: Glyph shown before the nation's insignia is set.

about.description: A sentence about the institution for the footer; the tagline when absent.

news.description: Announcements, newest first. Reference items are samples and carry no date.

newsSource.description: 'feed': taken from the ministry's existing website (Link, Embed or Migrate mode).

quickServices.description: The "I want to…" tasks; each opens a real service. Colour: a hex value or 'primary' / 'accent'.

statisticsSource.description: Where the figures come from. Reference figures are samples until the institution supplies its own.

translations.description: The published translations at this version, by language.

uptime.description: Hosted (or publisher) services counted for availability; planned maintenance excluded.

entity.description: Column holding the entity: its code (ISO 3166-2), its name, or the source's own id.

metric.description: Column holding the metric name, or a fixed metric for every row: a registered metric (lib/twin/metrics.ts).

unit.description: The unit as the source writes it; for a registered metric it must be that metric's UCUM unit (empty means that unit).

date.description: Column holding the date or year the value is true for, or one date for the whole file.

validTo.description: Optional: the date a value stops being true (interval facts, e.g. a budget year); empty means open-ended.

quality.description: Optional columns for the quality the source states: provisional, final or revised; a standard error; a 95% interval.

provisionedBy.description: Hosted nations get staging provisioned by the publisher.

StorePolicy.description: The store's business model, held as configuration (decided by the owner; see `decision`).

includedTier.description: 'free': the baseline is included and always on for every nation (decided); 'with-paid-tier' / 'paid' remain configurable.

certifiedVendorsOnly.description: The catalogue lists certified third-party vendors only (decided).

paths.description: Payment routes offered: government procurement and instant payment (both kept).

integrationId.description: The integration (Connected systems, scope sta:write) whose key may post this stream's readings through SensorThings.

StreamLineage.description: What a stream run read, for the run's lineage.

streamId.description: The substrate telemetry stream's id (a SensorThings Datastream id `telemetry:<id>` is read as the same stream).

entity.description: The twin entity the values describe (e.g. facility:FAC-00012, place:KE-30); default: the stream's facility.

metrics.description: Each registered metric and the daily statistic of the samples it records.

unit.description: The samples' unit as UCUM, when the stream's own unit text is not (e.g. "megawatts" → MW).

backfillDays.description: Days back the first run aggregates (default 7, at most 90).

channelKey.description: Private distribution link key: the nation's own feed and downloads.

history.description: Versions this nation ran before, most recent last (rollback target).

home.description: True for the nation this installation belongs to.

lkg.description: Last known good: the release that most recently passed probation.

language.description: The nation's language for release communication (the installed nation uses its setup language).

agentCredential.description: Deployment-agent credential metadata (the secret itself is shown once and never stored).

currency.description: Currency the nation is invoiced in, and the contract rate from the reference price list.

error.description: Why it is not running, or the last connection error.

link.description: The release or fallback incident the ticket is about.

tier.description: Contract tier at the time the ticket was opened: its targets apply.

waitingSince.description: The resolution clock pauses while the publisher waits on the nation.

coverage.description: When the desk answers, e.g. 24×7 or business hours.

uptimeTarget.description: Monthly availability target for hosted services, percent.

creditPct.description: Service credit when the monthly uptime target is missed, percent of the monthly fee (placeholder).

delta.description: A delta from the previous release, when the mirror already holds it.

link.description: The release or fallback incident the ticket is about.

tier.description: Contract tier at the time the ticket was opened: its targets apply.

waitingSince.description: The resolution clock pauses while the publisher waits on the nation.

code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 for the nation, ISO 3166-2 for subdivisions.

region.description: For places: the nation's operational region (setup) this is.

order.description: Its position in the nation's list of regions (official order).

uri.description: Its persistent identifier: https://<nation domain>/id/<kind>/<code>, resolved by /id/<kind>/<code> (entityUri).

fourEyesWithdrawal.description: Withdrawing an import needs a second official to confirm the proposal (default on).

privateBrokers.description: A stream's MQTT broker may resolve to a private or internal address (the nation's own network); default off.

withdrawn.description: Set when an official withdrew the import: its observations are superseded from that moment, never deleted. Under four-eyes, `by` confirmed what `proposedBy` proposed.

withdrawalProposed.description: A withdrawal proposed and waiting for a different official to confirm it (the nation's twin policy, lib/twin/policy.ts).

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the file as read (UTF-8 text), for provenance; absent on runs recorded before it was kept or that failed before reading. For a stream, of the samples read.

publisher.description: Who publishes it, e.g. "National Statistics Office".

kind.description: A CSV at an address or uploaded, or a substrate telemetry stream read as daily aggregates (lib/twin/stream.ts).

system.description: System name used in the crosswalk for this source's own entity ids.

format.description: The file's format: plain CSV with the mapping above (default), or SDMX-CSV 1.0/2.0, SDMX-JSON 2.0/1.0 or SDMX-ML 2.1 structure-specific data, read by lib/twin/sdmx.ts.

licence.description: The licence the publisher releases the data under (for the catalogue), when stated.

upgradePath.description: Release ids, in order, that take the installed version to the latest.

advisories.description: Halted or withdrawn releases this nation runs: falling back is advised.

UsagePolicy.description: What a partner may do with data received under a grant (ODRL-like; lib/exchange/usage-policy.ts).

purposes.description: Purposes the data may be used for (short words, e.g. "oversight", "statistics").

retentionDays.description: Days the partner may keep the data.

onwardSharing.description: Whether the partner may pass the data on to a third party.

WatchdogSummary.description: The watchdog. For every probation still running: fill in simulated health (prototype), treat a silent deployment agent as a failure, and pass the release when its window ends healthy. Never installs anything newer.

watching.description: Probations still running after this pass.

missingReports.description: Health reports recorded as missing in this pass.

locale.description: The nation's language and whether the notes are in it.

pending.description: True when the nation's language is not English and no translation exists yet.

placeHistory.description: Earlier places, oldest first (a place is moved or cleared, never overwritten silently).

receivedAt.description: When the case reached the institution; its age is counted from this. Absent on examples.

source.description: Where the case came from: an example of the platform, a loaded file, typed in, or a connected case system. Absent means example.

feedId.description: The connected case system (CaseFeed) that sent it; only that system updates it.

importId.description: The load (lib/data/case-import.ts) a case came in with.

actedAt.description: When an official last assigned, escalated or closed it.
